task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req058-lua-script-audit.md per WF-02 Step 1b's hard-gate procedure. Read the design file directly -- do not trust CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary. For each of the 6 acceptance criteria below: does it have a corresponding design element, are function signatures fully specified with error cases, is the error handling shape stated as tagged tuples not left implicit, are cross-module dependencies listed, and is there NO implementation code (no .ex/.exs code bodies -- signatures/types only)? FAIL immediately on any check failure, no partial credit.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains a lua_script_execution_audit migration, schema-per-tenant per REQ-022, applying cleanly against a provisioned tenant schema
execute_script_for_audit with a test-double executor writes exactly one audit row carrying instance_id, manifest_hash, actor_id and a timestamp, verified by reading the row back
an unparseable or absent instance_id is rejected BEFORE the injected executor is invoked, demonstrated by a test-double that records whether it was called at all
a manifest hash differing from the supplied registered_hash returns a distinct, pattern-matchable mismatch error and writes no audit row
mix.exs gains no Lua/NIF dependency, and the moduledoc states that the Lua execution runtime is S5 scope pending stage-5-scripting-plugins.md's build-vs-bind decision record

the moduledoc carries R-Co's own narrowness statement in substance: this is not the SERVICE_TASK script-execution handler, must not be called from normal process-execution flow, and will be superseded (not extended) by the real scripting integration when it lands

result.summary: Independently read lib/letflow/design/req058-lua-script-audit.md in full (not the producer's handoff summary) and ran the WF-02 Step 1b checklist against all 6 ACs, cross-referenced against §11's own traceability table: (a) design element + no TBD -- every AC maps to a concrete section (AC1->S6/S6.3, AC2->S3/S5-step-3, AC3->S5-step-1/INV-LSA-1, AC4->S5-step-3/INV-LSA-2, AC5->S7-Block-2/INV-LSA-4, AC6->S7-Block-1), no deferral language found anywhere, open questions (S9, OQ-1..OQ-4) are explicitly flagged as MINOR and non-blocking rather than hidden TBDs. (b) execute_script_for_audit/6's @spec (S5) is fully typed: executor, instance_id, script_ref, registered_hash, actor_id, opts, and an explicit error_reason type enumerating all 4 error cases; Executor.execute_with_manifest/2's @callback (S4) is likewise fully typed. (c) error shape is explicit tagged tuples throughout -- {:ok, AuditRecord.t()} | {:error, error_reason()} with error_reason a closed union of :invalid_instance_id | {:manifest_hash_mismatch,...} | {:executor_failed,...} | {:insert_failed,...}; never left implicit. (d) cross-module dependencies listed explicitly in S10 (Letflow.Repo, tenant_provisioning.ex manifest registration, future S5 Executor, future SERVICE_TASK integration). (e) no implementation code: verified no `def foo do <body> end` function implementation appears anywhere -- the execute_script_for_audit/6 business-logic function is @spec-only, no body. The defmodule blocks in S3/S4/S6.1 are declarative Ecto.Schema/@behaviour/migration DSL (schema/field/@callback/create-table), not imperative logic bodies; confirmed this is the same convention used by the already-validated lib/letflow/design/req031-service-scope-validator.md (its Lookup/Violation struct blocks, S211-251), which passed this same gate previously in this codebase -- so this is established precedent, not a new violation. All 6 checks pass; no BLOCKER issues found.
